newsitem.title: UK: Northern Electric pumps up bid defence.
newsitem.headline: Northern Electric pumps up bid defence.

text.p: Bid target Northern Electric Plc pumped up its defence on Tuesday with plans to merge its supply businesses with another regional electricity company (Rec) and raising its forecast for the year dividend to 50 pence a share.

The company, fighting off a 650 pence per share bid from U.S.-based CE Electric, said merging the businesses should achieve cost savings rising to over 28 million pounds ($46 million) a year and gearing was now forecast to be around 85 percent by March 2000.
Northern said it aimed to grow the dividend by at least seven percent from 1998 to 2000 and saw scope for real dividend growth from 2000 after the next price review.

Northern spent 560 million pounds on benefits to shareholders when it fought off a hostile bid from Trafalgar House, now part of Kvaerner, last year and said at the end of November that gearing should fall to around 95 percent by March 1997 against previous forecasts of 175 percent.
"Our new enhanced dividend policy reflects the underlying financial strength and prospects of Northern Electric. CE Electric's offer does not," chairman David Morris said.

CE Electric, which is 70 percent-owned by CalEnergy of the U.S., raised its offer from 630 pence per share on December 6 and drew a deadline of December 20, four days after a decision is expected from the UK government on whether the bid can proceed.
